sections.name: Chain Chomp (Bob-omb Battlefield)
sections.card:
Summary: A giant Chain Chomp chained to a peg in Bob-omb Battlefield, close to a cell that holds the Power Star of "Behind Chain Chomp's Gate".
Weak points: You cannot beat it, since Chain Chomps are almost entirely invincible, but a Bob-omb or a box stuns it for a moment.
Tips: It lunges at you when you are near and takes three wedges of health on contact. Ground-pound its post three times to free it, and it lunges into the nearby cell and clears the gate for the star.

sections.name: Boo (courtyard and Big Boo's Haunt)
sections.card:
Summary: A small ghost that follows you in the courtyard of Peach's Castle and in Big Boo's Haunt; touching one takes two wedges of health.
Weak points: A punch, a kick or a ground pound defeats it. When you look at one it turns partly see-through; otherwise it is solid and follows you.
Tips: Each Boo in the courtyard holds a yellow coin, and each one in Big Boo's Haunt holds a blue coin.

sections.name: Big Boo (Big Boo's Haunt)
sections.card:
Summary: The giant ghost who owns Big Boo's Haunt and leads the Boos; he is the boss of "Go on a Ghost Hunt", "Ride Big Boo's Merry-Go-Round" and "Big Boo's Balcony", and a touch costs three wedges of health.
Weak points: He can be hurt only while visible, by ground-pounding him from above or punching him from the side. Three hits defeat him, and he gets smaller and faster after each one.
Tips: In the first two missions you must defeat several nearby Boos to make him appear; in "Big Boo's Balcony" he is already there. Like a normal Boo he disappears when looked at and shows again when you turn away, and if you leave the area before he is beaten his health resets.
Tips: A Big Boo about twice the size of the other Boos waits in a corner of the castle courtyard, and beating it drops a birdcage that leads to Big Boo's Haunt.

sections.name: Piranha Plant (Whomp's Fortress)
sections.card:
Summary: A sleepy plant with green lips, found in Whomp's Fortress in the original game, that is always asleep, with a lullaby playing, until you disturb it.
Weak points: Walk up slowly and it stays asleep; touch it or rush at it and it wakes and bites toward you.
Tips: A bite takes three points of health, or four if you have lost your cap. A defeated Piranha Plant leaves a blue coin.

sections.name: Bob-omb (Bob-omb Battlefield)
sections.card:
Summary: A common walking bomb that first appears in Bob-omb Battlefield: when it spots you it lights its fuse and rushes at you.
Weak points: Touching one does no harm, but its explosion costs two wedges of health. Kick it, or pick it up from behind and throw it, and it explodes away from you and leaves a coin.
Tips: Their blasts also hurt other enemies nearby, and they come back after you leave the area.
Tips: A Bob-omb working a cannon does not chase you but still explodes if picked up; the pink Bob-omb Buddies are friendly, give hints and open cannons.

sections.name: Chuckya (Wet-Dry World, Tall, Tall Mountain and others)
sections.card:
Summary: A large purple Bob-omb variant that slides about on a metal point and charges you when you come in range; it patrols small areas in Wet-Dry World, Tall, Tall Mountain, Rainbow Ride, the huge side of Tiny-Huge Island and Bowser in the Sky.
Weak points: Pick it up from behind and throw it, and it explodes and releases five coins.
Tips: If it catches you it throws you in a random direction, sometimes a long way or into a pit. You can escape its grasp by pushing the Control Stick from the inside to the outside 11 times before it throws.

sections.name: Whomp (Whomp's Fortress)
sections.card:
Summary: A rock slab with an angry face that patrols a small area in Whomp's Fortress and falls on you when you get near; one more waits in Bowser in the Sky.
Weak points: Its only weak spot is its back: let it fall flat, then ground-pound it while it lies there, and it is defeated and releases five coins.
Tips: Landing on a Whomp's back releases a coin, up to five times. A trick in the original game lets you jump while it falls, pass through it and stand on its back.

sections.name: Mr. I (Big Boo's Haunt, Lethal Lava Land, Hazy Maze Cave)
sections.card:
Summary: A giant eyeball that turns to follow you and, if left alone, shoots small multicoloured bubbles at you; found in Big Boo's Haunt, Lethal Lava Land and Hazy Maze Cave.
Weak points: Run around it: it shrinks a little trying to keep track of you, is defeated, and drops a blue coin.
Tips: A larger Big Mr. I waits in the attic of Big Boo's Haunt.

sections.name: Tox Box (Shifting Sand Land)
sections.card:
Summary: A red metal box that rolls along set paths over a small tile maze in Shifting Sand Land, trying to flatten you.
Weak points: It cannot be defeated in the original game. One side of each box is a square hole: stand in it as the box passes over your tile and you survive, but the hole's edges still crush you if you stand under them.
Tips: Being squashed by a side costs three wedges of health. Long-jumping into a Tox Box's face over the quicksand loses a life at once, as if you had fallen into the quicksand. The maze has a few Red Coins and the course's only cannon.

sections.name: Power Star
sections.card:
Summary: The collectible star that clears a mission and opens more of the castle; there are 120 in the game.
Uses: The star doors and Big Star Doors in the castle need at least the number of Power Stars shown on them, and 70 are needed to enter Bowser in the Sky. Once you hold all 120, the cannon outside the castle opens and takes you onto its roof.
Tips: Each course holds seven Power Stars, one of them the secret star for 100 coins, and fifteen stars in all are Secret Stars hidden in secret areas or held by Toads. Eight red coins in a course make a star appear over a Star Marker.
Tips: A star you already have shows as a see-through blue copy, and collecting it adds nothing to your total.

sections.name: Red Coin
sections.card:
Summary: A red coin in Super Mario 64 is worth two yellow coins, and eight of them in one area make a Power Star appear over the nearby Star Marker.
Uses: The three cap-switch courses and the three Bowser courses each hold eight, and the two secret courses The Secret Aquarium and Wing Mario Over the Rainbow have one star each from their red coins. The Princess's Secret Slide is the only course with none.
Tips: The red coin missions by course: Bob-omb Battlefield, Find the 8 Red Coins; Whomp's Fortress, Red Coins on the Floating Isle; Jolly Roger Bay, Red Coins on the Ship Afloat; Cool, Cool Mountain, Frosty Slide for 8 Red Coins; Big Boo's Haunt, Seek the 8 Red Coins; Hazy Maze Cave, Elevate for 8 Red Coins; Lethal Lava Land, 8-Coin Puzzle with 15 Pieces; Shifting Sand Land, Free Flying for 8 Red Coins.
Tips: The rest: Dire, Dire Docks, Pole-Jumping for Red Coins; Snowman's Land, Shell Shreddin' for Red Coins; Wet-Dry World, Go to Town for Red Coins; Tall, Tall Mountain, Scary 'Shrooms, Red Coins; Tiny-Huge Island, Wiggler's Red Coins; Tick Tock Clock, Stop Time for Red Coins; Rainbow Ride, Coins Amassed in a Maze.

sections.name: Blue Coin
sections.card:
Summary: A darker blue coin worth five yellow coins.
Uses: Most come from ground-pounding a Blue Coin Block, and they last only a limited time: once the timer runs out they cannot be collected. Some defeated enemies drop one: Koopa Troopas, Piranha Plants, Boos, Mr. Is, Bookends, Pokeys and the Small Koopa Troopa, and a Grand Goomba gives one only if you kill it with a ground pound.
Tips: The blue coins on the slides in Cool, Cool Mountain (one) and Tall, Tall Mountain (three) start to move away from you as you get close, unlike still yellow coins.

sections.name: 1-Up Mushroom
sections.card:
Summary: A mushroom with a green cap and yellow spots that gives an extra life.
Uses: You find them on top of poles, in some yellow blocks, by touching butterflies that are not explosive, in a small field of flowers, and by flying through a ring of coins.
Tips: Some stand still, some move away from you and some move at you. Three sit on the roof of the castle.

sections.name: Koopa Shell
sections.card:
Summary: A rare green shell in Super Mario 64 that you can ride for fast travel.
Uses: Jump on it to travel fast and ram enemies, which defeats them instantly. Riding a shell lets you cross water, lava, quicksand and deadly quicksand without sinking or being hurt, and holding one underwater lets you swim faster for a short while.
Tips: Shells come from hitting some yellow blocks or from attacking a Koopa Troopa to knock it out of its shell. In the original game the blocks do not refill, but a shell stays until you ride it.
Tips: In the Nintendo 64 version of Tiny-Huge Island you can ride the shell on the wind over the Windswept Valley.

sections.name: Cannon
sections.card:
Summary: Blue cannons in ten courses and one secret stage fire you to places you cannot normally reach, but each stays covered until you find and talk to that course's Bob-omb Buddy.
Uses: Drop into the hole to climb in, aim with the targeting reticle and press the button to fire. Aim slightly higher than your target, and you take no falling damage from the shot. With a Wing Cap on, you can fly at once after the shot without a triple jump.
Tips: Cannons cannot be unlocked until the first mission is done. In Bob-omb Battlefield one cannon can never be used because it shoots water bombs.
Tips: In the Whomp's Fortress mission "Blast Away the Wall" you shoot yourself out of a cannon to smash the top of a nearby wall and free the star.
